---
title: "Reporting a problem"
date: 2026-09-30
---

If something on `bioconductor.org` is broken, slow, missing or different from before,
report it, however small. Everything goes through one place, the issue forms in the
bioc-infrastructure repo, so you don't need to know which part of the system is at fault.

## Where to report

| Problem | Where |
|---|---|
| A package won't install, can't be found, or a download fails | [Package install problem](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues/new?template=install-problem.yml) form: the command you ran, the full output, your setup, and where you install from (bioconductor.org or a mirror) |
| A page, download, redirect or file on bioconductor.org doesn't work | [Something's broken on bioconductor.org](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues/new?template=site-problem.yml) form: the URL, what happened and what you expected, how you accessed it, the output or a screenshot, and when you noticed |
| A suspected security problem | Email, never a public issue; see [Security](#security) |
| Questions about these docs, corrections, anything else | [bioc-infrastructure issues](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues), or email [seandavi@gmail.com](mailto:seandavi@gmail.com) |
| How to use a package | The [Bioconductor support site](https://support.bioconductor.org) |
| The wording of a page on bioconductor.org | [Bioconductor/bioconductor.org issues](https://github.com/Bioconductor/bioconductor.org/issues); the prose still lives there |

A page that looks out of date may be a stale copy at the edge. The
[edge cache](cache.qmd) page shows how to tell from the response headers; report it either
way, with those headers if you have them.

## How triage works

- Both forms add the `report` label, which means "incoming, not yet triaged".
- One person triages reports by hand: Sean Davis, who operates the new stack
  ([operations](operations.qmd#who-operates-what)). No response time is promised and there
  is no on-call rotation.
- A report is moved to the repo that owns it
  (bioc-edge for serving, caching and the sync; bioc-website for how pages render;
  bioc-registry for the registry), or fixed with a linked pull request and closed here. For
  example, [#47](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues/47) (the About page
  showing HTML as code) was filed on 2026-09-29 and closed the same day by
  [bioc-website#32](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-website/pull/32).

On 2026-09-30, three reports were open
([`label:report`](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3Areport)).
A written triage protocol and automated first-pass triage are planned in
[bioc-infrastructure#43](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues/43), not built.

## Security {#security}

Report vulnerabilities privately by email to Sean Davis
([seandavi@gmail.com](mailto:seandavi@gmail.com)), as
[bioc-edge's SECURITY.md](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-edge/blob/main/SECURITY.md)
describes. It says to expect a reply within a few days and asks you to allow time for a fix
before public disclosure. The same route applies to problems found in the legacy
bioconductor.org infrastructure; the maintainer coordinates disclosure with the Bioconductor
core team. Don't open a public issue for either.
